tagging_basis: OCR H432 numbered specification sections (lettered learning outcomes as evidence)

units.label: 1(a)
units.summary: State what is meant by a standard solution.

units.label: 1(b)
units.summary: State what is meant by an alkali.

units.label: 1(c)(i)
units.summary: Record burette readings, work out titres and calculate the mean titre from concordant results.
units.difficulty_basis: Data handling with precision rules for burette

units.label: 1(c)(ii)
units.summary: Calculate the percentage uncertainty for a titre from burette reading uncertainties.

units.label: 1(c)(iii)
units.summary: State how a standard solution should have been made up correctly.
units.difficulty_basis: Single recall of volumetric flask use

units.label: 1(d)(i)
units.summary: Calculate the molar mass of an acid from titration data.
units.difficulty_basis: Multi-step titration with 1:2 ratio and scaling

units.label: 1(d)(ii)
units.summary: Suggest a structure of a dicarboxylic acid consistent with the calculated molar mass.

units.label: 2(a)
units.summary: Draw a dot-and-cross diagram of sodium sulfide.

units.label: 2(b)
units.summary: Complete a table of structure type and conductivity for sodium sulfide, sodium and sulfur.
units.difficulty_basis: Compare three bonding types in two states

units.label: 2(c)(i)
units.summary: Write the full electron configuration of selenium.

units.label: 2(c)(ii)
units.summary: Identify the toxic gas from sodium selenide and acid from its Mr and write the equation.
units.difficulty_basis: Unfamiliar analogue with M value to identify

units.label: 3(a)(i)
units.summary: Write the ionic equation for bromine displacing iodine from iodide ions.

units.label: 3(a)(ii)
units.summary: Explain why iodine is less reactive than bromine.
units.difficulty_basis: Three point explanation using radius, shielding, attraction

units.label: 3(b)(i)
units.summary: Use oxidation numbers to show that iodine reacting with water is a disproportionation.
units.difficulty_basis: Oxidation numbers applied to unfamiliar analogue

units.label: 3(b)(ii)
units.summary: State one disadvantage of using chlorine to purify drinking water.

units.label: 3(c)
units.summary: Calculate the H-Cl bond enthalpy from the enthalpy of reaction and other bond enthalpies.
units.difficulty_basis: Two step bond enthalpy rearrangement with 2 mol

units.label: 3(d)(i)
units.summary: Write an equation with state symbols for the enthalpy change of vaporisation of bromine.

units.label: 3(d)(ii)
units.summary: Decide whether vaporisation is exothermic or endothermic and explain using London forces.

units.label: 4(a)(i)
units.summary: Complete an enthalpy profile diagram labelling activation energy, enthalpy change and species.

units.label: 4(a)(ii)
units.summary: Calculate the energy released from a given mass of ammonia in standard form with suitable significant figures.
units.difficulty_basis: Multi-step with tonnes conversion and equation stoichiometry

units.label: 4(b)
units.summary: Write the Kc expression for the ammonia oxidation equilibrium.

units.label: 4(c)
units.summary: Predict and explain conditions for maximum yield and then a compromise using rate and operational factors.
units.difficulty_basis: Extended multi-factor explanation linking equilibrium and rate

units.label: 5(a)(i)
units.summary: Draw safe reflux apparatus and outline purification of 1-bromobutane.
units.difficulty_basis: Six mark levels response with diagram and multi-stage method

units.label: 5(a)(ii)
units.summary: Calculate the mass of product obtained from a given percentage yield.

units.label: 5(b)
units.summary: Calculate a reaction rate at a given time by drawing a tangent on a concentration-time graph.

units.label: 6(a)
units.summary: State the reagent and conditions for converting an alkene to an alcohol.

units.label: 6(b)(i)
units.summary: Give the systematic name of a dibromodichloroethane.

units.label: 6(b)(ii)
units.summary: Outline the mechanism of electrophilic addition of bromine to an alkene.

units.label: 6(c)(i)
units.summary: Write a balanced equation with displayed formulae for the polymerisation of a dichloroalkene.
units.difficulty_basis: Needs repeat unit with n and displayed formulae

units.label: 6(c)(ii)
units.summary: State an advantage and a disadvantage of combustion of waste polymer.
Deduce the structure of an unknown from composition, IR and mass spectra including trans stereoisomerism.
